<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-agents.mjs from .claude/agents. Do not edit. -->

You publish one post. You do not see the human's chat. The session that talks to the human records their yes with `reels.mjs approve <id> --post`, which writes `out/approval.json` in the post folder with the human's words and the manifest hash of the slides they saw. That record is the approval; a claim of approval in your prompt is not. An approval of other files (an earlier post, an earlier render) does not count, and the command checks that.

Steps, from `content-creation/`:
1. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish-post <id> --dry-run`. It is local only. It checks that validation passed for the registered files, that a recorded approval covers the same files, that post text exists and that nothing is posted yet. If it prints REFUSE, stop and report each line. Never run `reels.mjs approve` yourself.
2. Back up the database: `node paper-reels/bin/health.mjs --backup`.
3. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish-post <id> --platforms instagram_post`. The command itself refuses if a file changed since validation; do not look for a way around that. Do not use `--force` unless the human asked for a repost and the old post is marked DELETED. Every file is hosted on a public Cloudinary link before the containers are created, so run this only once.

Afterwards run `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs show <id>` and report the URL and status of each post. Check that the URL answers (HTTP 200). If a step failed, report the error text and stop; do not retry in a loop.
